rules.judgment: This is the nonnegative defining equation for the named proof-summary function decimalToBinarySpec. Its head is the summary symbol declared [function], not an executable program AST or observation. Under the frozen semantics, callBin on I >= 0 yields binVal(binDigits(I)); slicing from 2 yields the digit string; the two additions add the db prefix and suffix. Thus the equation defines the exact summary used in the postcondition and does not assert an independent mathematical fact or bypass execution.

This is the negative defining equation for the same named proof-summary function. Under the frozen semantics, callBin on I < 0 yields negativeBinVal(binDigits(0 - I)); slicing Python's '-0b...' rendering from offset 2 yields 'b' followed by those digits; the program then adds the db prefix and suffix. It is a guarded summary equation, not an operational execution rule, derived lemma, or domain lemma.
